title: The benefits of agile
blurb: Recognize the three benefits of being and doing agile that PRINCE2 Agile describes, and what produces each one.
question: A director wants the organization to cope with sudden market changes while keeping work focused on its strategic objectives. Which benefit of agile, as described in PRINCE2 Agile, is she looking for?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile sets out the benefits an organization gains from being agile and doing agile. Three are the ones to know for the exam: organizational resilience and alignment; more efficient teams and engaged people; and responsiveness and innovation. Each has a cause you can recognize in a question stem, so learn the benefit together with what produces it.

Agile teams are ready to navigate change and adjust their approach, while still prioritizing work that contributes to organizational objectives. That makes the organization more resilient: better equipped to face uncertainty and respond to unforeseen challenges, while keeping its focus on the most valuable outcomes. Resilience is about coping with change; alignment is about pointing the work at the objectives.

teach.h: More efficient teams and engaged people
teach.body: Collaboration and transparent communication within cross-functional teams make work flow more efficiently. Empowering teams to self-manage and make decisions builds trust, ownership and a strong sense of purpose, which in turn lifts morale and productivity. Look for stem words such as 'trust', 'ownership', 'morale' or 'self-manage'.

Agile organizations put learning first. They use feedback loops to reflect on successes and challenges, and that commitment to continual improvement helps teams refine processes, reduce waste, stay flexible and develop innovative solutions to complex problems. Stem words: 'feedback loops', 'reflect', 'continual improvement', 'innovative'.

teach.h: Spot the benefit from its cause

teach.body: Ashgrove Community Health is building a clinic-booking service. When funding rules change mid-year, product owner Kwame Asante reorders the backlog towards the new priority without derailing the project: resilience and alignment. The team chooses how to split its own work, and morale rises: engaged people. Retrospectives cut rework and produce a new self-check-in idea: responsiveness and innovation.

teach.text: Do not mix up a benefit with a success factor or a product. Psychological safety (2.7.4) and the change management approach (4.2.1) are not among these 2.4 benefits. And 'engaged people' comes from empowering teams to self-manage, not from closer supervision.

items: Resilience and alignment: adapt to change while prioritizing work that serves organizational objectives.
Efficient teams and engaged people: collaboration, transparency and self-management build trust, ownership, morale and productivity.
Responsiveness and innovation: feedback loops and continual improvement reduce waste and produce innovative solutions.
The benefits come from being agile as well as doing agile; a framework alone does not deliver them.

summary: You can now name the three benefits of agile that PRINCE2 Agile describes and link each to its cause. That lets you match a question's description to resilience and alignment, efficient and engaged teams, or responsiveness and innovation.

A.q: Agile teams navigate change while prioritizing work that serves organizational objectives. Which benefit of agile does this describe?
options: Responsiveness and innovation
More efficient teams and engaged people
Organizational resilience and alignment
Psychological safety across the teams
A.why: Adapting to change while prioritizing work that contributes to organizational objectives is organizational resilience and alignment (2.4).

whyNot.0: Responsiveness and innovation comes from feedback loops and continual improvement.
whyNot.1: Efficient teams and engaged people comes from collaboration and self-management.
whyNot.3: Psychological safety is a success factor for agile (2.7.4), not one of these benefits.

A.q: Empowering teams to self-manage and make decisions leads to which benefit of agile?
options: More efficient teams and engaged people
Organizational resilience and alignment
Responsiveness and innovation
A stronger change management approach
A.why: The book links self-management to trust, ownership, purpose, morale and productivity: more efficient teams and engaged people (2.4).

whyNot.1: Resilience and alignment is about adapting while serving organizational objectives.
whyNot.2: Responsiveness and innovation comes from feedback loops and continual improvement.
whyNot.3: The change management approach is a PRINCE2 management product, not a benefit of agile.

A.q: Using feedback loops to reflect on successes and challenges, and improving continually, produces which benefit?
options: Organizational resilience and alignment
More efficient teams and engaged people
A fixed and predictable scope
Responsiveness and innovation
A.why: Feedback loops and continual improvement help teams reduce waste and develop innovative solutions: responsiveness and innovation (2.4).

whyNot.0: Resilience and alignment is about adapting while keeping work aligned to objectives.
whyNot.1: Efficient, engaged teams come from collaboration and self-management.
whyNot.2: Agile flexes scope; a fixed scope is not one of its benefits.

B.q: Why are agile organizations more resilient, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: They fix scope early and so avoid change
They are better equipped to face uncertainty
They rely less on business justification
They add approval layers to each decision
B.why: Agile organizations are better equipped to face uncertainty and respond to unforeseen challenges (2.4).

whyNot.0: Resilience comes from adapting to change, not avoiding it.
whyNot.2: Business justification still matters; resilience does not come from reducing it.
whyNot.3: Extra approval layers slow adaptation and reduce resilience.

B.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, what does empowering teams to self-manage foster?
options: Stricter control of the work by line managers
Longer and more detailed team plans
Less need for collaboration across the team
Trust, ownership and a sense of purpose
B.why: The book says empowering teams to self-manage fosters trust, ownership and a strong sense of purpose, lifting morale and productivity (2.4).

whyNot.0: Self-management reduces the need for close line control rather than increasing it.
whyNot.1: Self-management is not about producing longer plans.
whyNot.2: Agile teams rely on close collaboration; self-management does not reduce it.

B.q: Which way of working most directly makes agile teams more efficient?
options: Collaboration and open communication in cross-functional teams
Separate specialist teams handing work to one another in turn
Detailed instructions issued to each person by a manager
Keeping the status of work private until it is finished
B.why: The book links collaboration and transparent communication in cross-functional teams to more efficient teams (2.4).

whyNot.1: Handovers between specialist silos are what cross-functional teams avoid.
whyNot.2: Detailed direction from a manager is the opposite of self-management.
whyNot.3: Hiding status works against the transparency agile relies on.

C.q:
Which two are benefits of agile described in PRINCE2 Agile?
1. Organizational resilience and alignment.
2. Removal of the need for a project board.
3. Responsiveness and innovation.
4. Scope agreed in full at the start.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 3
C.why: Resilience and alignment (1) and responsiveness and innovation (3) are benefits named in 2.4.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: PRINCE2 Agile keeps the project board and its governance.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: the board remains, and agile flexes scope rather than fixing it all at the start.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: agile flexes lower-priority scope.

C.q: At Ridgeway Print, a team reflects on each iteration in retrospectives, cuts rework and designs a new way to proof jobs online. Which benefit is this, and what drives it?
options: Resilience and alignment, driven by fixed plans
Engaged people, driven by close supervision
Responsiveness and innovation, driven by feedback
Responsiveness and innovation, driven by long phases
C.why: Reflecting through feedback loops and improving continually produces responsiveness and innovation (2.4).

whyNot.0: The scenario is about learning and new solutions, and fixed plans do not drive that.
whyNot.1: Engagement comes from self-management, and the scenario describes innovation, not supervision.
whyNot.3: The benefit is right, but it comes from short feedback loops, not long phases.

C.q: Which statement about the benefits of agile is correct, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: They come from adopting a framework on its own
They come from being agile as well as doing agile
They depend on removing project governance
They appear once all requirements are fixed
C.why: The syllabus frames these as the benefits of being agile and doing agile; the book warns that a framework by itself guarantees nothing (2.3, 2.4).

whyNot.0: This is the misconception the book warns about (2.3).
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control throughout.
whyNot.3: Fixing all requirements up front works against agile's adaptability.

reteach.title: Three keywords, three benefits
reteach.question: How can you match a stem to the right benefit in seconds?

blocks.body: If the stem talks about coping with change while staying focused on organizational objectives, think resilience and alignment. If it talks about trust, ownership, morale or teams deciding for themselves, think efficient teams and engaged people. If it talks about feedback loops, reflection, continual improvement or new solutions, think responsiveness and innovation.

blocks.text: Psychological safety, agile maturity and the change management approach are real topics, but they are not the three 2.4 benefits.

explain.body: Teams adapt to change while prioritizing work that serves organizational objectives, so the organization copes better with uncertainty and stays focused on the most valuable outcomes (2.4).

test.q: Which benefit lets an organization respond to unforeseen challenges while focusing on its most valuable outcomes?
options: Organizational resilience and alignment
More efficient teams and engaged people
Responsiveness and innovation
Agile maturity across the teams
test.why: Responding to the unforeseen while focusing on the most valuable outcomes is resilience and alignment (2.4).

whyNot.1: This benefit is about collaboration, self-management and morale.
whyNot.2: This benefit is about feedback loops and new solutions.
whyNot.3: Agile maturity is a key metric for agility (2.7.6), not one of these benefits.

explain.body: Collaboration and transparent communication in cross-functional teams improve efficiency. Self-management builds trust, ownership and purpose, raising morale and productivity (2.4).

test.q: A team that is allowed to decide how it works reports higher morale and productivity. Which benefit is this?
options: Organizational resilience and alignment
More efficient teams and engaged people
Responsiveness and innovation
Continued business justification
test.why: Self-management fosters trust, ownership and purpose, which lift morale and productivity (2.4).

whyNot.0: Resilience and alignment concerns adapting while serving objectives.
whyNot.2: Responsiveness and innovation concerns feedback loops and improvement.
whyNot.3: Continued business justification is a PRINCE2 principle, not an agile benefit.

explain.body: Feedback loops let teams reflect on what went well and what did not. Continual improvement reduces waste, keeps teams flexible and produces innovative solutions to complex problems (2.4).

test.q: What produces the benefit of responsiveness and innovation, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Detailed plans agreed at the very start
Strict adherence to a single framework
Feedback loops and continual improvement
Larger teams with more specialist members
test.why: The book links feedback loops and a commitment to continual improvement to responsiveness and innovation (2.4).

whyNot.1: Rigid adherence to a framework is not how agile creates value.
whyNot.3: Team size is not what the book links to this benefit.

explain.body: These benefits come from being agile (the mindset, with freedom to apply it) as well as doing agile (frameworks and techniques). Adopting a framework alone does not guarantee them (2.3).

test.q: A company adopts an agile framework but keeps managers approving every team decision. What is it likely to miss?
options: The benefit of engaged, self-managing teams
The use of agile terminology in meetings
A set of timeboxed iterations for delivery
A prioritized backlog of user stories to build
test.why: Without freedom to self-manage, the company does agile without being agile, so it misses benefits such as trust, ownership and morale (2.3, 2.4).

whyNot.1: It already has the terminology; that is part of doing agile.
whyNot.2: Timeboxed iterations come with the framework it adopted.
whyNot.3: A backlog is part of the framework it has adopted.
